name: manual_b19ffe
claim: After orama-system's history is rewritten, verify a specific commit's content survived by diffing its tree against origin's current tree (git show <sha>:<path> | diff), not by trusting commit-graph ancestry (merge-base/ahead-behind) or the reanchor_scan classification alone.

decisions.notes: Session hit 'multiple merge bases' + 600+ commits diverged on each side of local main, on exactly the files just fixed and pushed. reanchor_scan.sh correctly flagged it as a tree-twin situation, but the decisive proof that no work was lost was a direct git show/diff of the function body between the local commit SHA and origin/main's current tree — content-identical despite different SHAs. Ahead/behind counts alone would have wrongly suggested real divergence needing a merge.
